answers.reason: Charashim (H2798) names the craftsmen’s valley in 1 Chronicles 4:14; Ge-harashim explicitly includes the alias 'valley of Charashim' and that verse.
Tarpelites (H2967) are a people mentioned in Ezra 4:9. No candidate is supplied.
Jegar-Sahadutha (H3026) is Laban’s Aramaic name for the witness heap called Galeed by Jacob in Genesis 31:47. No candidate is supplied.
Jehovah-jireh (H3070) names the site of Abraham’s sacrifice in Genesis 22:14. No candidate is supplied.
Jehovah-shammah (H3074) is the name assigned to Ezekiel’s envisioned city in Ezekiel 48:35. Jeshanah is a separate settlement mentioned in 2 Chronicles 13:19.
Chidon (H3592) identifies the threshing floor where Uzzah died in 1 Chronicles 13:9. None of the candidates identifies that threshing floor; Kidron is a different name and a river.
Carmelite (H3761) is the gentilic of the town Carmel, used for Nabal in 1 Samuel 30:5. The settlement candidate also carries 'Carmelitess'; Mount Carmel is a separate geographical referent.
Maktesh (H4389) is the district addressed in Zephaniah 1:11, generally understood as a quarter of Jerusalem. None of the candidates represents that district.
Miphkad (H4663) names a gate of Jerusalem in Nehemiah 3:31. The candidates are separate settlements or a wilderness campsite.
Mesobaite (H4677) is Jasiel’s gentilic in 1 Chronicles 11:47. Neither Nebaioth nor Mesopotamia is an equivalent referent; the resemblance is only in spelling.
